sermon.title: Jesus Teaches on swearing — July 7, 2022
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Jesus taught it is best not to swear at all. Herod kept a wicked oath and was only sorry; Peter swore falsely, wept in remorse and was restored. As Numbers 30 foreshadows, Christ our Father and husband can overrule failed vows so we can start anew.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Welcome and worship led by others until 30:45. Spoken references as given: “Matthew 33 verse 34” (5:34).

faqs.question: What are ways to worship?
faqs.answer: Lifting and clapping hands, instruments, standing, bowing, dancing, shouting, singing.

faqs.question: Did people come for miracles?
faqs.answer: He says they came to hear His teaching.

faqs.question: Is it a sin not to vow?
How long can police take to arrive?
Could Herod give half his kingdom?
faqs.answer: It wasn’t his to give; Rome ruled.

faqs.question: Is it enough for parents to be sorry?
faqs.answer: No, not if they don’t change.

faqs.question: Is guilt good?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it moves you to repent and let Christ overrule it.

faqs.question: Did he ever fall asleep praying?
What did he promise when filled with the Spirit?
faqs.answer: To read the Bible through every year.
